maria_docs: Heads-up — I just noticed the Python SDK snippet in the Optimize toolkit docs produces unexpectedly long completions for short prompts when paired with the `qprofile-shortseq-v1` quant profile. Repro steps + snippet below. Opening a PR now but wanted to flag here first.

arjun_eng: can you paste the snippet and the model + profile you used?

maria_docs: Sure. Repro (local):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(model='rw-open-7b', quant_profile='qprofile-shortseq-v1', prompt='hi')
print(resp.text)
```
This returns a ~120-token completion for a 1-token prompt; expected ~5-12 tokens.

lee_eng: hmm, that sounds like the profile is falling back to a looser temperature/penalty default somewhere. Do you have the full payload or SDK-generated request body?

maria_docs: The SDK request body shows `max_tokens: 128` (default), `temperature: 0.8` (from profile), `presence_penalty: 0`. The docs example omits `max_tokens` which makes the example rely on defaults that our quant profiles influence.

arjun_eng: That explains it — for short prompts we recommend forcing `max_tokens` <= 32 in the snippet or adding an explicit guidance comment. The `qprofile-shortseq-v1` intentionally sets higher temperature for diversity but docs shouldn't accidentally ship that as an unconstrained example.

samira_pm: TL;DR: docs example needs a small-note about `max_tokens` and a link to the short-sequence migration guide. If we change the sample, let's also call out recommended `quant_profile` mapping for conversational vs. short-turn tasks.

maria_docs: I'm drafting PR #5124 with two changes: 1) update the Python snippet to set `max_tokens=16`, 2) add a short paragraph under "Quant profiles and prompt length" advising defaults, 3) fix a broken anchor link to the migration guide (link currently 404).

lee_eng: If you want I can add a short unit test in the docs CI that runs the snippet with a mock client to ensure the sample prints a short completion (sanity check).

maria_docs: Please do — that would prevent regressions.

arjun_eng: Also double-check the JS snippet in the same page. We had one earlier that used `max_tokens` but with different units (`max_tokens: 0.05` mistaken type) — likely a copy bug.

maria_docs: Good catch. I'll sweep both Python + JS.

deploy-bot: Deploy preview created for branch `docs/shorttok-fix-5124` — https://deploy-preview-5124.redwood-internal.dev (expires in 72h) :rocket:

samira_pm: Can we add a short table: "When to use: qprofile-shortseq-v1 vs qprofile-default" — one line each. Helps customers pick without reading the full eval doc.

maria_docs: Adding that now. Also adding an explicit note about `streaming` behavior with quantized models — there was confusion in support tickets.

lee_eng: For the test, I'll add a mocked response where `generate` returns 8 tokens. We'll fail the CI if the example output > 32 tokens. PR link once you push?

maria_docs: Pushed. PR #5124 is open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5124 — includes snippet changes + anchor fix + short table.

arjun_eng: Reviewed and left a couple of nit comments about wording and a code comment that explains why `max_tokens=16` for short-turn examples. LGTM otherwise.

maria_docs: Thanks — addressed comments and updated the preview.

docs-bot: Note: automated link-checker found the migration guide anchor renamed from `#shortseq-migration` to `#short-token-migration` — updated anchor and added redirect in the site config.

samira_pm: Great. Can we also add a one-line note in the migration guide about batch/caching interactions for short prompts? Some customers saw worse latency when caching prefixes of size 1.

lee_eng: I'll add a short appendix to the migration guide on caching heuristics (prefetch aggressively only when typical seq_len > 8).

maria_docs: Ok, PR merged. Closing this thread after we verify the docs CI and deploy preview. Thanks everyone :heart:

lee_eng: Thanks all.

samira_pm: :tada:
